constraints: The control must be a part of its target.
No separate button: the gesture happens on the content itself.
It must work with one finger and no hover.
The result must leave a physical trace.
Use only one material.
Two materials must collide at the moment of commit.
The control's shape changes for good after use.
Make the dangerous version slower, not redder.
The rehearsal shows exactly the first 20 percent of the effect.
The state must be readable from the silhouette alone.
It must look different on the 50th use.
It must read correctly in grayscale.
The control looks at the user as they approach.
Use depth instead of color.
Use gravity.
The undo is the remnant.
Make it a tool, not a switch.
Borrow from a craft older than 100 years.
Count with objects, not numbers.
Let the user's past actions show in it.
Reverse the expected direction, then justify it.
A seven-year-old must understand it.
A seventy-year-old must understand it.
No icons allowed anywhere in it.
Use the edge of the screen.
It must still work at 24 pixels.
The surface itself is the control.
Waiting is part of the meaning.
Say it with light only.
Design the sound first, then the smallest visual that matches it.
Use a phase change.
The rest pose tells the whole story.
Tie it to the time of day.
The second press feels different from the first.
It must be satisfying to do slowly.
It must be impossible to trigger by accident.
The target answers before the control moves.
It must work on a surface you can't scroll.
Remove one channel, then make it clearer anyway.
Use a mechanism, not a metaphor.
Show the cost before the commit.
Make the empty state the invitation.
Let it be imperfect, like something handmade.
The fluent version must take half the time.
Combine two seeds that don't belong together.
